title: Europe's IPO backlog almost halves, but AI could yet refill it
excerpt: The pool of European IPO listing candidates has substantially shrunk this year, even as the window remained open. AI companies are expected to drive the next...
content_html:
Kelsey Rees

Wed, August 5, 2026 at 7:57 AM EDT 2 min read

The pool of European IPO listing candidates has substantially shrunk this year, even as the window remained open. AI companies are expected to drive the next wave.

PitchBook's latest analyst note on Europe's IPO window shows that a favorable combination of low volatility, supportive valuations, and a stable interest rate policy has aided listing volumes, with 87 listings so far this year, and Q2 counts up 28.9% quarter-over-quarter.

This article appeared as part of The Europe Pitch newsletter. Sign up here

At the same time, the backlog of potential listings has almost halved. Only 223 companies in Europe now have a high probability of going public, a 40.2% slump from the 373 businesses noted in PitchBook's 2025 outlook.

Just 10 of those companies have more than a 90% probability of an IPO, down from 32 a year ago.

Moreover, their combined valuation totals roughly €232 billion (about $268 billion), with only one company, Revolut, accounting for most of it at €200 billion.

The remaining pipeline's composition is broadly similar to 2025, though UK organizations saw the largest declines in IPO candidates, alongside biotech and pharma companies. Germany and software also had notable decreases in their pipeline counts.

The future of the IPO pipeline may lie in artificial intelligence, with AI firms representing a third of candidates. Europe has 72 AI IPO candidates, including seven with a 90% or higher probability of listing on the public markets.

The top AI firms by valuation span verticals including robotics and drones (defense), Big Data, cybersecurity, agricultural technology, and fintech.

By country, 37.5% of European AI IPO candidates sit in the UK, followed by 18.1% in France and 8.3% in Germany.

PitchBook expects the share of AI IPO candidates to continue to rise as Europe's AI ecosystem matures, suggesting the next generation of IPOs is likely to be more technology-led than the last.

This article originally appeared on PitchBook News

content_html_zh:
凯尔西·里斯

2026 年 8 月 5 日星期三，美国东部时间上午 7:57 阅读 2 分钟

尽管窗口仍然敞开，但今年欧洲 IPO 上市候选人的数量已大幅缩减。 人工智能公司有望推动下一波浪潮。

PitchBook 关于欧洲 IPO 窗口的最新分析师报告显示，低波动性、支撑性估值和稳定利率政策的有利组合有助于提高上市量，今年迄今已有 87 家上市，第二季度环比增长 28.9%。

本文作为欧洲推介时事通讯的一部分出现。 在这里注册

与此同时，潜在上市的积压几乎减少了一半。 目前，欧洲只有 223 家公司有很高的上市可能性，比 PitchBook 2025 年展望中提到的 373 家公司减少了 40.2%。

其中只有 10 家公司 IPO 的可能性超过 90%，低于一年前的 32 家。

此外，它们的总估值总计约为 2,320 亿欧元（约合 2,680 亿美元），其中仅 Revolut 一家公司就占了大部分，达 2,000 亿欧元。

剩余管道的构成与 2025 年大致相似，尽管英国组织以及生物技术和制药公司的 IPO 候选人下降幅度最大。 德国和软件业的管道数量也显着减少。

IPO管道的未来可能在于人工智能，人工智能公司占候选人的三分之一。 欧洲有 72 家人工智能 IPO 候选企业，其中 7 家在公开市场上市的概率为 90% 或更高。

按估值排名的顶级人工智能公司涵盖机器人和无人机（国防）、大数据、网络安全、农业技术和金融科技等垂直领域。

按国家划分，欧洲人工智能 IPO 候选人中有 37.5% 来自英国，其次是法国，占 18.1%，德国占 8.3%。

PitchBook 预计，随着欧洲人工智能生态系统的成熟，人工智能 IPO 候选人的比例将继续上升，这表明下一代 IPO 可能比上一代更加以技术为主导。
